info.title: Custom Signals API
info.description: Signals produced by custom signal definitions — signal types defined as data (out of stealth, new office or market entry, first or founding hire, …) rather than the four built-in families. One endpoint serves every definition; `type` selects which. A free companion endpoint lists the definitions, and a team can create, start, pause and remove definitions of its own.

get.description: Fetch signals produced by custom signal definitions, with filtering, pagination and search. Filter by `type` (definition slug, comma-separated), confidence floor, keyword, dates, company identifiers and HQ country. Every row carries the definition, a headline, verbatim evidence quotes from the post and the definition-specific `attributes`. Custom signals are social-post evidence: they are not corroborated by a second source the way funding rounds are — use `min_confidence` to tighten.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100)

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: `false` skips the full-cohort count: `pagination.totalCount` and `totalPages` come back null and the page is faster.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Return only the total count that matches the filters (`data` is empty). Free of charge.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Definition slug(s), comma-separated. Omitted = every definition. Find slugs with GET /signals/custom/definitions. A malformed slug is a 400; an unknown but well-formed slug matches nothing.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: Search phrase that found the post (partial match)

parameters.name: min_confidence
parameters.description: Extractor confidence floor, 0 to 1

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across headline, summary and company name

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Filter signals from this date (ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD), on occurredAt

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Filter signals up to this date (ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD), on occurredAt

parameters.name: date_preset
parameters.description: Relative date shorthand — takes precedence over dateFrom/dateTo

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Company HQ allowlist: comma-separated ISO codes, names or regions (EU, DACH, …)

parameters.name: exclude_countries
parameters.description: Company HQ denylist: comma-separated names or codes. Unknown HQ is kept.

parameters.name: subcategories
parameters.description: Comma-separated subcategory IDs

parameters.name: company_domain
parameters.description: Recommended. Company website domain (single or comma-separated up to 50). Strict match; scheme, www. and trailing slash are ignored.

parameters.name: company_linkedin_url
parameters.description: Recommended. LinkedIn company URL. Strict match.

parameters.name: company_name
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive company name. Prefer the URL identifiers.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Sort field

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction

parameters.name: filter_version
parameters.description: Filter compatibility version. Omit for current behaviour; 1 freezes legacy matching; 2 enables strict country validation.

get.description: The definitions you can filter GET /signals/custom by: every global definition plus your own team's. Free of charge — it is the catalogue, not data. Each entry's `slug` is the value to pass as `type`; `description` is the rule a post must satisfy to count; `attributes` names the definition-specific fields its signals carry.

post.description: Create a definition of your own from a name and a plain-English rule. Signalbase compiles the rule into search phrases and a matching rule and test-runs it against recent posts; the definition moves compiling → testing → ready over a few minutes. Poll Retrieve Definition until it is ready, review the test leads, then start it with Update Definition (`active: true`). Nothing is swept until it is started. With `targets` the definition only watches those companies; without, it sweeps every post. Free (0 credits). A team may hold 3 definitions (paused ones count, removed ones do not); the feature needs a Pro plan.

example.name: First sales leader
example.description: The author's own company announces hiring its first sales leader or is building its first sales team: a first VP Sales, Head of Sales, CRO or founding account executive. Exclude ordinary sales hires at companies that already have a sales team, and recruiter posts about other companies.

Starting a definition that is still compiling, testing or failed is a 400. Free (0 credits).

bearerAuth.description: API key authentication. Include as Bearer token in Authorization header.

type.description: The definition slug (e.g. stealth_exit, new_office, founding_hire). Same value as definition.slug.

occurredAt.description: The event date when the post stated one, otherwise when the post was published.

headline.description: One line stating the signal as a fact.

confidence.description: The extractor's confidence in the match.

keyword.description: The search phrase that found the post.

sourceUrl.description: The post the signal was extracted from.

attributes.description: Definition-specific fields (e.g. location, kind for new_office; role, function, stage for founding_hire). Null when the post did not state them.

evidenceQuotes.description: Verbatim quotes from the post that support the signal.

occurredOn.description: The event date as stated in the post, if any.

slug.description: Pass as `type` on GET /signals/custom, or in a monitor's signal_types.

description.description: The rule a post must satisfy to count.

status.description: Global definitions are active or disabled. Your own walk compiling → testing → ready → active, and can be paused, disabled or failed.

TestLead.description: One post the test run matched. The leads of a ready definition become its first signals when it is started.

headline.description: The event, stated as a fact.

TestRun.description: The last test run: how many recent posts were fetched and classified, how many matched, and the matches themselves.

mode.description: restricted when the definition has targets.

companiesChecked.description: Restricted runs only: how many of the targets were checked.

OwnDefinition.description: One of your team's own definitions, as the Custom signals page shows it.

slug.description: Derived from the name and made unique with a short suffix. Pass it as `type` on GET /signals/custom or in a monitor's signal_types.

description.description: The compiled rule a post must satisfy. Written by the compile step from sourceDescription; empty until compiled.

sourceDescription.description: What you sent as `description` when creating it.

status.description: compiling: search phrases and a rule are being derived. testing: a test run is in flight. ready: tested, not started; review test.leads. active: running. paused: kept, not swept. failed: see compileError. disabled: removed.

attributes.description: The definition-specific fields its signals carry (set by the compile step).

keywordCount.description: How many search phrases the compile step produced.

restricted.description: true when the definition only sweeps its targets' posts (through a monitor).

monitorId.description: The monitor that holds the targets of a restricted definition.

lastRunAt.description: When the sweep last ran this definition.

nextStep.description: What to do next, given the status.

attached.description: Create only: how the targets resolved. null when the definition is global.

seeded.description: Update with active:true, first start only: how many test leads became signals.

name.description: A short name for the signal, e.g. "First sales leader". The slug is derived from it.

description.description: What a post must say for it to count, as a plain-English rule about the author's own company: the event, what makes it that event and not a neighbour of it, and anything to exclude. Two or three sentences. Compiled into search phrases and a matching rule — write the rule, not a keyword list.

targets.description: Company website domains or LinkedIn company URLs. Given, the definition only sweeps posts from these companies (a monitor watching the new slug holds them); omitted, it sweeps every post. `companies` is accepted as an alias.

active.description: true starts a ready or paused definition (a first start makes its test leads its first signals); false pauses an active one. Other transitions are a 400.

DefinitionSlug.name: slug
DefinitionSlug.description: The definition's slug, as returned when it was created or by the catalogue.
